raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Find a bench near the children's play area, watch them play à la française, and listen — the Hebrew, Yiddish and Arabic around you sit oddly with the fact that this was, for nearly two centuries, the single most fashionable square in Paris.","source_id":"4cfc4c1b-d0e7-440b-9b60-b25adefc3987","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"If it's cold, there's Café Ma Bourgogne at the northwest corner, where the view through the window is nearly as good.","source_id":"4cfc4c1b-d0e7-440b-9b60-b25adefc3987","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Just off the northeast corner, at 36 rue des Tournelles, one woman ran the salon the richest and sexiest of Paris couldn't stay away from.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Her name was Ninon de l'Enclos, born in 1620, and like every Frenchwoman of her century she had exactly four paths open to her: wife, nun, prostitute, or governess.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"She tried the convent, lasted a year, and came home to host what became a fabled literary salon.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"She was determined not to marry, and lived instead as a famous courtesan, taking many lovers — nobles, and even the priests and bishops who denounced her from the Sunday pulpit.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"What galled the Church wasn't the courtesan so much as the author who openly scorned organized religion.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Molière adored her; he wrote that 'she has the keenest sense of the absurd of anyone I know.'","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"His play Les Précieuses Ridicules — The Pretentious Young Ladies — mocked the idle chatter of the salons and the sycophants who filled them.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The pious Queen Anne of Austria had Ninon locked in a convent for a few months — more for her influence than for her scandalous love life.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"'Feminine virtue,' she said, 'is nothing but a convenient masculine invention.'","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Her guests hung on lines like that; the memoirist Saint-Simon sat among them, taking notes.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"And when she died in 1705, she left money to a boy she'd once met at the age of nine — Voltaire — to buy books.","source_id":"b7206637-67c1-4ef2-9b77-ab1238dee5f1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That's Place des Vosges — the most fashionable square in Paris, and the corner where Ninon kept her salon.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0}]}
